Facilities & Operations Manager
We are currently seeking to fill two key positions with a reputable organisation operating within Papua New Guinea’s property and commercial sector.
About the Company
Our client is a well-established organisation within the property and commercial sector, recognised for delivering high-quality property management and operational services. With a strong industry reputation, the company is committed to maintaining safe, efficient, and professionally managed facilities while continuing to support business growth and operational excellence.
About the Role
These are exciting opportunities for experienced Facilities & Operations Managers to join a high-performing team and play a key role in overseeing property operations, maintenance activities, and site management across multiple locations.
Working closely with senior management, the successful candidates will oversee daily facilities operations, coordinate maintenance activities, supervise contractors and site teams, and ensure all properties are maintained to the highest standards of safety, presentation, and operational efficiency.
Key Responsibilities
Manage daily facilities and operational activities across multiple properties and sites
Supervise maintenance teams, contractors, and suppliers to ensure work is completed safely and efficiently
Conduct regular property inspections to ensure compliance with company standards and maintenance requirements
Develop and manage preventative maintenance schedules to minimise downtime and operational disruptions
Coordinate manpower, tools, materials, and resources to support operational activities
Review and approve maintenance reports, inspection checklists, and work orders
Ensure all maintenance and operational documentation is accurate and submitted on time
Monitor contractor performance and ensure service delivery meets company expectations
Troubleshoot operational and maintenance issues and implement effective solutions
Provide regular operational updates and reports to senior management
Ensure workplace health, safety, and compliance standards are maintained at all times
Support continuous improvement initiatives to enhance operational efficiency and property standards
Requirements
3–5 years’ experience in facilities management, operations, property management, or a similar role
Strong knowledge of building maintenance systems, construction site operations, and property management practices
Trade qualification or demonstrated hands-on experience in electrical, plumbing, HVAC, carpentry, or general maintenance
Strong leadership and team management skills with the ability to supervise multiple teams and contractors
Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting abilities
Strong organisational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Ability to prepare reports, schedules, and operational documentation
Proven ability to coordinate operational activities and meet deadlines
How to Apply
To apply, interested candidates are requested to submit:
A cover letter addressing the key criteria of the role
An updated CV in Microsoft Word format outlining employment history, qualifications, and three professional referees

26835.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As the
Advisor, Mechanical
– Shovels & Drills
at Lihir Operations, you will provide critical mechanical and maintenance expertise that supports safe, reliable, and efficient asset performance. Your technical advice and hands‑on support will directly contribute to operational uptime, continuous improvement, and the capability development of the national workforce.
Working closely with Maintenance and Operations teams, you will play a key role in troubleshooting, risk management, and process optimisation while ensuring strict adherence to safety and compliance standards.
As part of our team, you will
Provide hands‑on technical support to Maintenance and Operations teams to resolve mechanical issues and improve asset performance
Coach and mentor the national workforce in maintenance, troubleshooting, and safe work practices
Support the investigation, diagnosis, and resolution of complex technical problems
Analyse operational and maintenance data to identify trends, risks, and improvement opportunities
Conduct regular inspections and audits to ensure compliance with safety, quality, and technical standards
Work closely with the maintenance team to coordinate equipment repairs and manage critical spares
Assist in the design, preparation, and delivery of technical training programs
Develop and provide practical recommendations to improve maintenance processes and reliability outcomes
Manage and monitor inventory for critical spare parts and equipment
Identify technical risks, implement mitigation measures, and continuously monitor risk controls
Stop unsafe work and actively always promote a strong safety culture
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Mechanical Trade Certificate or Degree in Mechanical Engineering
Proven experience maintaining heavy mining equipment (shovels, excavators, drills)
Demonstrated expat experience mentoring and developing a national workforce
Strong practical capability in troubleshooting, machine diagnostics, maintenance support, and process optimisation
Proven experience working within strict safety and compliance frameworks
The ability to analyse data and translate findings into actionable improvements
Sound risk identification and mitigation skills
Strong communication skills with the ability to coach, influence, and work collaboratively across disciplines
A proactive mindset, practical judgement, and commitment to continuous improvement
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 21:21 Day / Night Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster from PNG or Australia approved point of hire to Lihir Island, PNG.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Apply

Credit Corporation PNG is recruiting a suitable candidate for the role of
Technology Risk Specialist.
The Technology Risk Specialist is responsible for conducting risk- analysis and reporting of information obtained from multiple sources such as system generated transactions, IT monitoring applications and other risk registers.
The Technology Risk Specialist will collaborate with the relevant business units within Credit Corporation as part of the second line risk function ensuring that technology risk controls are embedded and tested to be operating effectively.
The role reports into the Head of Enterprise Risk Management and acts as a risk business partner to the IT team. The role is based in Port Moresby.
Primary Responsibilities:
Help oversee and implement risk mitigation programs, controls and governance in relation to technology risk
Regularly undertake reviews of IT risks to ensure the IT risk register is current and reflective of the business environment
Undertake 2nd line control tests to ensure effectiveness and works with the first line to remediate where needed
Manage IT Risk Appetite Statements reporting in collaboration with the IT team
Report on issues and execute governance programs to ensure actions are closed within deadlines
Investigate, escalate and report IT related incidents ensuring the identified control gaps are remediated
Collaborate with the IT team to ensure disaster recovery readiness from a second line perspective
Provide advisory to stakeholders on IT risk management practices
Provide IT risk reporting to management and the board as required
Operate as second line defense to ensure technology risk is managed within appetite
Coordinate enterprise-wide IT risk awareness programs
Collaborate with the IT team for the management of IT related policies and procedures
Other Duties
Other duties as directed or required by the Head of Enterprise Risk Management or Chief Risk Officer
Key Overall Competencies
Must have a bachelor's degree in IT, Computer Science or IT risk related discipline
Formal Qualifications
Mandatory:
Bachelor's degree in IT or Computing Science
IT or Information security risk management certification advantageous – CRISC, CISA, CISM, ISACA etc
Knowledge required:
Banking or risk reporting knowledge
Prior IT governance or risk reporting experience is desirable
Advanced MS Excel and proficiency with other data management tools
Experience with Protecht system advantageous
Knowledge of risk and data governance fundamentals
Experience:
Minimum 3yrs in risk management, Information Technology or compliance
Banking, IT or risk reporting experience is advantageous
Sound knowledge of Technology and Cyber security regulations and industry standards
Advanced MS suite skills and proficiency with data management tools
Experience with developing and reviewing policies
Prior experience in banking or finance is an advantage
Knowledge of cloud technologies is an advantage
Self-starter and experience working across teams and stakeholders
Prior experience working with IT risk and governance policies desirable
Prior experience in IT projects advantageous

26987.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.
About the role
This position is responsible for carrying out electrical breakdown and preventative maintenance repairs on a wide range of mobile equipment’s including Light Vehicles, Boggers, Truck fleet, Excavators, Drills, Dozers, Graders, and support equipment.
Key Accountabilities
Performing scheduled and Breakdown maintenance on a large fleet of Underground Mining Equipment including Sandvik Drills, Trucks and Loaders with an ancillary fleet of CAT and Normet equipment.
Conduct regular electrical tests and tagging on equipment’s and machines.
Direct and train subordinates to install, maintain or repair electrical wiring, equipment’s, and machines.
Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you must have a NATTB certified Trade certificate in Auto-electrical with at least 3-5 years of relevant work experience in heavy industry preferably mining environment. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Demonstrated experience in maintaining electrical equipment in the mobile fleet including Drills, Trucks, Loaders as well as Light vehicles, Dozers, excavators, graders,
Relevant experience in automotive air conditioning systems.
Self-motivated with ability to always work autonomously.
Strong safety focus and sound knowledge of standard operating procedures.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply

26443.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
In this role you will provide management and leadership within our mobile maintenance department. This rewarding role will see you provide daily mentoring, guidance, instruction, and training to the national workforce to increase safety performance, machinery uptime and efficient outcomes within a motivated and talented department.
Key Accountabilities
Coordinate workshop activities through the Mobile Maintenance Supervisors.
Give direction, delegate tasks and provide technical assistance to subordinates.
Liaise with senior maintenance leadership on planned maintenance.
Maintain stock levels and place orders as required.
Ensure cost control measures are considered by utilizing resources available to full capacity.
Report and rectify any hazardous sightings to the Mobile Maintenance Superintendent in the 800L workshop.
Ensure training requirements are met.
Organise and document weekly safety toolbox meetings workshop safety representatives.
Regularly monitors and evaluates staff performance in consultation with Mobile Maintenance Superintendent.
Provide coaching for performance improvement.
In conjunction with mobile maintenance superintendent, takes disciplinary action to address performance deficiencies, in accordance with the Company’s rules, policies and procedures.
Personally, responds to inquiries and complaints from the employees.
Responds to emergency situations as necessary.
Carry out other relative duties as directed by the Mobile Maintenance Superintendent.
Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.
About You
Qualifications & Experience
Relevant trade qualification in Heavy Equipment Fitting, Auto Electrical and Automation. Minimum Certificate III required.
10+ years relevant work experience essential.
Underground mobile fleet such as Sandvik and Caterpillar and provide guidance of Methods, practices, techniques.
Ability to plan, assign, direct and coordinate a variety of functional specialties (areas) with overlapping work areas.
Must have at least 5 years in mobile fleet maintenance in a supervisory capacity. Should also have experience in training of both operating and maintenance personnel.
Experience in the use of Pronto will be advantageous.
Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent trouble shooting skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply

27300.description:
Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources & Environment (PNGUNRE)
The Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources & Environment invites applications from suitably qualified and experienced professionals for the position of Human Resources Business Partner (HRBP) within the Registry Division.
PNGUNRE is undergoing a period of institutional transformation aimed at strengthening governance, operational efficiency, compliance, and service delivery. The University is seeking a highly competent and results-oriented HR professional to support strategic organisational reform and institutional strengthening initiatives.
About the Role
Reporting directly to the Registrar, the Human Resources Business Partner (HRBP) will provide strategic and operational leadership in strengthening the University’s human resource management systems, organisational structures, governance frameworks, and administrative processes to support institutional performance excellence.
The successful candidate will work closely with the Vice Chancellor, Senior Management Team, and key stakeholders including the Department of Personnel Management (DPM), to modernise HR systems, improve organisational effectiveness, and support the implementation of the University’s strategic priorities.
Key Responsibilities
The successful candidate will be responsible for:
Strategic Human Resource Management
Leading the review and strengthening of HR management systems and practices.
Providing strategic HR advisory support to senior management.
Supporting workforce planning, succession planning, and talent management initiatives.
Developing strategies to improve organisational culture, accountability, productivity, and staff performance.
Organisational Review & Institutional Strengthening
Reviewing organisational structures, staffing establishments, and reporting frameworks.
Supporting implementation of recommendations arising from organisational and DPM reviews.
Reviewing job descriptions, classifications, and accountability frameworks.
Identifying operational inefficiencies and recommending improvement measures.
Assisting with institutional performance reviews and strategic planning processes.
HR Policy, Compliance & Administration
Reviewing and updating HR policies, procedures, and manuals in line with PNG labour laws and Public Service General Orders.
Improving employee records management systems and HR documentation standards.
Strengthening recruitment, onboarding, probation, disciplinary, leave, and separation processes.
Supporting audit readiness and institutional compliance initiatives.
Performance Management & Capacity Building
Assisting in the development of integrated performance management systems.
Developing HR operational templates, tools, and reporting mechanisms.
Conducting training, mentoring, and capacity-building programs for managers and supervisors.
Strategic Planning & Change Management
Supporting the implementation of the University’s Strategic Plan and operational plans.
Facilitating organisational change management initiatives.
Promoting professionalism, accountability, service excellence, and continuous improvement across the University.
Qualifications & Experience
Essential Requirements
Applicants must possess:
A Bachelor’s degree in Human Resource Management, Organisational Psychology, Business Management, Public Administration, or a related discipline.
A minimum of ten (10) years’ senior-level experience in human resources and organisational development.
Demonstrated experience in organisational review, strategic planning, change management, and institutional strengthening.
Strong understanding of PNG Public Service systems, General Orders, and employment legislation.
Experience working with government agencies, universities, statutory bodies, or large organisations.
Strong report writing, facilitation, stakeholder engagement, and communication skills.
Competency in the use of computerised systems and applications.
Desirable Qualifications
Preference will be given to applicants with:
Postgraduate qualifications in HR, Management, Organisational Development, or related fields.
Experience in higher education institutional reform.
Experience in salary structure reviews, workforce planning, and performance management systems.
Training, coaching, or consultancy experience.
Key Competencies
The ideal candidate should demonstrate:
Strategic thinking and planning capability
Leadership and organisational influence
Strong organisational development and change management skills
Policy development and implementation capability
High level interpersonal and communication skills
Integrity, professionalism, and accountability
Strong analytical and problem-solving ability
Project management capability
Ability to work independently and deliver outcomes within agreed timelines
Terms & Conditions
The appointment is on a fixed-term contract for twelve (12) months.
Performance will be assessed against agreed deliverables and milestones.
The successful candidate may be required to conduct workshops, training, and consultations across campuses and departments.
A competitive remuneration package will be negotiated based on qualifications and experience.
Why Join PNGUNRE?
PNGUNRE offers an exciting opportunity to contribute meaningfully to institutional transformation and organisational strengthening within Papua New Guinea’s higher education sector. The successful candidate will play a key role in shaping systems, structures, and strategies that support long-term institutional excellence.
Application Details
Interested applicants should submit:
A written application addressing the selection criteria;
A current curriculum vitae (CV);
Certified copies of qualifications;
At least three (3) current referees with contact details.
Applications should be addressed to:
The Registrar
Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources & Environment
Private Mail Bag,
Kokopo, East New Britain Province, PNG
Or email applications to:
[email protected]
Closing Date:
10th of June 2026
PNGUNRE is an equal opportunity employer. Female applicants and suitably qualified Papua New Guineans are strongly encouraged to apply.
Apply

27225.description:
Position Title
:      Customs Clearance Manager
Company Name:
Carpenter Agricultural & Manufacturing Ltd (T/A
Globe
)
Location:
Madang
Job Overview
We are looking for an experienced and detail-oriented
Customs Clearance Manager
to lead our import and export operations from our Madang base. In this role, you will be the driving force behind seamless, compliant, and cost-effective cargo clearance across PNG ports — ensuring our supply chain keeps moving and our business stays ahead.
Key Responsibilities
Manage end-to-end import and export clearance through the Papua New Guinea Customs Service, coordinating with licensed brokers, shipping lines, and freight forwarders.
Ensure full compliance with the Customs Act 1951, ASYCUDA World declarations, IRC tax requirements, and NAQIA quarantine regulations.
Review and approve all import/export documentation — including commercial invoices, bills of lading, packing lists, and import permits — and ensure accurate HS code classification.
Act as the primary liaison with PNG Customs officials, port authorities, quarantine bodies, and regulatory agencies to facilitate timely cargo release.
Monitor vessel arrivals and container movements, proactively managing demurrage, port storage, and clearance costs to avoid congestion-related expenses.
Identify and mitigate compliance risks including documentation gaps, potential penalties, and operational disruptions at port.
Supervise the customs clearance team and coordinate closely with warehouse, procurement, and logistics functions to align shipment planning with clearance readiness.
Negotiate service rates with brokers and logistics partners, and maintain audit-ready records for internal and external reviews.
Required Qualifications & Skills
Diploma or Degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
Minimum 3–5 years of customs clearance or freight forwarding experience in Papua New Guinea.
Demonstrated working knowledge of the PNG Customs Act 1951 and the ASYCUDA World system.
Strong understanding of HS code classification, customs valuation, GST, and import duty frameworks.
Experience liaising with PNG Customs Service, IRC, NAQIA, and port authorities.
Proficient in reviewing shipping documentation and identifying discrepancies before lodgement.
Strong negotiation skills with brokers, freight forwarders, and logistics service providers.
Solid computer literacy including MS Office; experience with logistics or ERP systems is an advantage.
Desired Personal Qualities
Reliable and accountable — you take ownership of outcomes and follow through on commitments.
Sharp attention to detail with the ability to manage complex documentation accurately under pressure.
Proactive communicator who builds strong working relationships with government bodies and internal teams.
A calm problem-solver who can navigate port delays, regulatory changes, and unexpected operational challenges.
Professional, ethical, and discreet in handling sensitive business and compliance matters.

Accounts Payable (AP) manages a company's short-term financial obligations, ensuring vendor invoices are accurately verified, coded, and paid on time
. Key duties include processing invoices, reconciling statements, managing expense reports, and maintaining vendor relationships. This role requires high attention to detail and proficiency in accounting software.
Core Responsibilities and Duties
Invoice Processing:
Receiving, approving, and coding invoices for payment, ensuring they match purchase orders and contracts.
Payment Execution:

Reconciling processed work by verifying entries and comparing system reports to vendor statements.
Vendor Management:
Acting as the primary point of contact for vendor inquiries, resolving payment discrepancies, and maintaining updated vendor records.
Expense Reporting:
Reviewing employee credit card statements and expense reports for policy compliance.
Record Keeping:
Maintaining accurate, up-to-date, and organized historical records for auditing purposes.

Technical Skills:

Studied accounting or finance preferred.

27251.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a
Supervisor – Asset Management
, you will lead your team to safely deliver planned production outputs while maintaining high standards across
safety, quality, and performance
. Your leadership will directly influence team culture, operational efficiency, and plant reliability across a complex
fixed plant environment
.
You will play a key role in driving proactive safety behaviours, developing team capability, and ensuring maintenance activities are executed effectively across
crushing, grinding, flotation, and associated process plant systems
. Through strong leadership and decision-making, you will support business targets while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Lead and promote a strong safety-first culture through visible leadership, coaching, and safety interactions
Deliver agreed production and maintenance outcomes in line with plans and Superintendent expectations
Set clear goals and performance standards for your team aligned with operational strategy
Supervise, coordinate and assign daily tasks to ensure work is completed safely and efficiently
Monitor team performance, ensuring compliance with procedures, policies, and safe systems of work
Provide ongoing coaching, mentoring, and performance feedback to build team capability
Engage and collaborate with peers, planners, and support teams to achieve site objectives
Participate in shift handovers, reporting, and maintaining accurate records of key events
Identify, escalate, and manage risks, delays, and operational issues impacting performance
Drive cost efficiency, identifying opportunities for savings and minimising waste
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Minimum Grade 12 education with a Mechanical Trade Qualification (essential), NATTB Trades Certificate in Maintenance Fitting highly regarded
Current PNG Driver’s Licence
3–5 years’ experience in fixed plant maintenance, ideally within mining or heavy industry, with demonstrated progression into leadership or supervisory responsibilities
Proven experience leading teams in a safety-critical environment, including conducting safety interactions, coaching, and incident reporting/investigation
Strong hands-on experience in mechanical maintenance, including fitting, machining, fabrication, pump rebuilds, pipe fitting, and HDPE welding
Solid technical knowledge of hydraulic systems, pumps, valves, crushers, mills, and conveyor systems
Strong understanding and application of safe systems of work, PNG Mine Safety Act, and site HSE frameworks
Demonstrated ability to plan, prioritise, and supervise work, ensuring quality and productivity targets are met
Effective communication, leadership, and interpersonal skills with the ability to engage and influence diverse teams
Proven ability to coach, develop, and manage performance while fostering a positive and accountable team culture
High level of organisational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage competing priorities in a dynamic environment
Proactive approach to problem-solving, continuous improvement, cost control, and waste reduction
Ability or willingness to obtain mobile equipment tickets (e.g. forklift, gantry crane
Your Work Environment
This role is offered on a
28:14 Day / Night Fly in, Fly out (FIFO)
roster to Lihir Island, PNG.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Beyond work, you’ll enjoy the best of tropical island living, with access to a vibrant range of social and recreational activities. Our comprehensive relocation program ensures a smooth transition into the local community, including cultural orientation, international-standard schooling (see more at
https://lisstm.com.au/)
, quality healthcare services, and household support.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Apply

Islands Petroleum
(IP) is an independently owned fuel and lubes distributor, and the exclusive distributor for Mobil lubricants in Papua New Guinea. With the head office based in Kokopo,
Islands Petroleum
also operates bulk fuel depots in Rabaul, Kimbe, Konebada, Kavieng, Alotau, Popondetta/Oro Bay and Mt. Hagen as well as lubes and fuel distribution warehouses in Lae, Port Moresby, and Madang.
We are currently seeking to hire an experienced
Commercial Analyst
to join our growing team, the successful candidate will be based at our Head office in Port Moresby, NCD.
The Role & Responsibilities
A Commercial Analyst evaluates business operations, sales performance, and market trends to provide actionable insights that drive profitability and inform decision-making. They analyze data, develop financial models, and create reports on sales, margins, and trends to guide company strategy and support stakeholder decision-making.
Provide commercial and analytical support across Islands Petroleum assets.
Conduct market research and pricing, and performance analysis.
Support new business opportunities and business development initiatives.
Collaborate with project teams and key stakeholders on commercial matters.
Prepare reports, reporting dashboards, presentations, and commercial documentation.
Customer pricing, tender pricing and ICCC monthly system price change.
Develop and execute retail fuel pricing strategies to maximize profitability, often setting prices across multiple locations.
Market monitoring - Track product costs, competitor pricing, and economic indicators to stay ahead of market volatility.
Prepare daily, weekly, and monthly reports on product margin and volume performance for management and sales teams.
Work with sales and operations teams to coordinate pricing, ensure system compliance, and implement best practices.
Candidate Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in economics, Finance, Commerce, Business, or related field.
Minimum 5 years’ experience in the oil and gas industry, resource sector or related field.
Experience in Customer Relationship Management (CRM) and financial analysis.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Professional, accountable, and results driven.
Excellent time management and organizational skills.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
High level of confidentiality and ethical conduct.
Why choose Islands Petroleum?
At Islands Petroleum, we believe our employees are our greatest asset. We are committed to creating a workplace where employees feel valued, supported, and empowered to grow both professionally and personally. We offer:
A safe, inclusive, and respectful working environment
Competitive remuneration and employee benefits
Opportunities for career growth, learning, and development
A culture built on teamwork, integrity, and accountability
Recognition and rewards for performance and contribution
Work-life balance and employee wellbeing support
The opportunity to make meaningful contributions to the business and community
At Islands Petroleum, we do not just offer jobs, we provide opportunities to build rewarding careers and be part of a team that drives success together.

27006.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
This position is part of a team responsible for the implementation and maintenance of the mine power supply and distribution system for all electrical equipment on the mine and exploration sites in Kainantu.  In addition, this position will also play and important role in the training of trades assistants.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Inspect, isolate, and repair electrical malfunctions using various hand and power tools.
Ensure that alarms and emergency electrical systems onsite are always operational.
Direct and train subordinates to install, maintain or repair electrical wiring, equipment, and machines.
Ensure and maintain safe work standards and practices in accordance with mine safety regulations for all tasks performed.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you are a NATTB certified electrician, with PPL certification and demonstrated experience within a mining / minerals processing environment. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Experience in installation and maintenance of power distribution systems, transformer installations, motor control Centre’s, LV and HV transfers and starters.
The ability to fault find and develop appropriate solution in order to ensure the equipment availability is high.
Maintain current electrician’s license to meet government regulations.
Ability to train maintenance personnel in all aspects of their trade – particularly in diagnosis and fault finding, quality control, thoroughness and record keeping.

About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
The New Porgera Limited now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our Capital and Projects as
Supervisor, Senior - Community Projects Tax Credit Scheme.
About the role
The role is responsible for managing and delivering community projects across designated areas, ensuring they are completed safely, efficiently, and in line with agreed cost, quality, and schedule. Reporting to the Superintendent – Community Projects, the position focuses on driving project delivery excellence while maintaining compliance with company policies, regulatory requirements, and sustainability standards.
In this role, you will:
Deliver building, civil and road construction projects and community projects within approved cost, quality, and schedule
Plan, coordinate, and manage project activities across remote and dispersed locations

Manage project budgets, ensuring effective cost control and financial accountability

Ensure all projects comply with company policies, government regulations, and industry standards

Maintain high standards of health, safety, and environmental compliance

Monitoring building projects, systems and business processes as well as identify and prioritize improvement opportunities to formulate alternatives and improvements to systems and methods
Ability to coordinate and manage projects to achieve completion to agreed quality, budget and schedule
Ensure that building, civil and road construction and community projects comply with NPL policy for sustainability, government requirements and guidelines
Ability to manage projects spread over a large and remote area
Ensure development and maintenance of up-to-date job procedures for all tasks performed within the team
Ensure appropriate facilities, procedures and workforce competence to achieve legal compliance, incident prevention and the achievement of tasks in an environmentally sustainable manner
Being responsible for the safe and efficient operation of the team

About You

Current PNG Driving License Class 6

27215.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As Superintendent Mine Planning, you will be responsible for developing and overseeing mine plans across time horizons ranging from two years to one day, ensuring alignment with long‑term strategies, production goals, and regulatory requirements. Your leadership will shape the accuracy, efficiency, and integrity of mine planning processes, driving continuous improvement, strengthening operational performance, and supporting safe, responsible mining. You will play a central role in coordinating planning activities, guiding technical teams, and delivering high‑quality insights that enable informed decision‑making across the operation.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Lead the preparation and execution of Monthly, Weekly, and Daily mine plans to support operational delivery.
Develop and oversee <2‑year mine plans (Business Plan and Quarterly Forecast) to ensure alignment with the 5‑Year Plan, production targets, and regulatory obligations.
Manage reconciliation reporting across daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual horizons to track performance against plan and support strategic objectives.
Drive continuous improvement through mine design updates, block model refinements, financial and operational input reviews, and fleet assessments.
Provide direction, support, and influence to mine operations to enhance operational effectiveness while ensuring compliance with safety standards and mining regulations.
Lead and develop a team of 25, coordinating training, capability development, and proactive Fatal Risk Management processes to identify, mitigate, and monitor risks.
Prepare scopes of work, manage budgets, and oversee mine planning consultants and contracts, ensuring adherence to project specifications, safety standards, and organisational goals.
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Bachelor’s degree in Mining Engineering or a related discipline (essential).
Advanced proficiency in mine design, drill and blast, mine scheduling, and performance‑to‑plan reconciliation.
Strong understanding of mine operations, dispatch systems, risk management, and business improvement principles.
Demonstrated experience in project and/or contract management.
Proven leadership capability with experience managing and developing technical teams.
Familiarity with mining software and cost‑modelling tools; advanced proficiency in mine planning and optimisation software (Deswik and MineSight highly regarded).
Strong problem‑solving ability, including the capacity to analyse complex information, identify patterns, and make effective decisions.
Well‑developed social process skills, including self‑awareness, collaboration, conflict resolution, and the ability to foster an inclusive, high‑performance team environment.
Commitment, determination, and follow‑through to deliver productive outcomes aligned with Newmont’s purpose, values, and desired culture
Your Work Environment
You’ll be part of a dynamic mining operation at our Lihir site, collaborating closely with internal teams across mine operations, geology, processing, asset management, and technical services, as well as engaging with external consultants and contractors. The role combines office-based planning with field-based oversight.
The role is offered on a
Residential
basis with a
5:2 roster
, or on a
FIFO
basis from approved points of hire within Australia and Papua New Guinea, operating on an even-time
21:21 roster
.
Beyond work, you’ll enjoy the best of tropical island living, with access to a vibrant range of social and recreational activities. Our comprehensive relocation program ensures a smooth transition into the local community, including cultural orientation, international-standard schooling (see more at
https://lisstm.com.au/)
, quality healthcare services, and household support.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Apply

Spectra Industrial Limited - a Leader in Sales, Service and Hire of Forklifts, Gensets and Industrial Supplies, is seeking organized and well experienced individuals to join our Lae Spare Parts Team and be a part of our growing enterprise!
Position Description
Position Title: Accounts Receivable Officer
Company: Spectra Industrial
Location: Lae, Papua New Guinea
Reports To: Financial Controller
Position Purpose
The Accounts Receivable Officer is responsible for timely invoicing, debtor collections, account reconciliations, and maintaining accurate customer account records. The role supports cash flow by monitoring outstanding balances, resolving billing issues, preparing receivables reports, and ensuring receivables processes comply with company policies and relevant Papua New Guinea financial and tax requirements.

Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.
Effective communication and interpersonal skills.
Mechanical knowledge and technical understanding of forklifts and heavy equipment.
Ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced operational environment.
Strong focus on customer service, accuracy, and operational efficiency.

Experience with invoicing, debtor collections, reconciliations, ageing reports, and customer account maintenance.

27233.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The FE Maintenance Advisor is the senior technical authority. responsible for overseeing the entire work management process to ensure maintenance activities are prioritised, planned, scheduled, and executed to the highest standard. This role provides leadership to Technical Advisors & Supervisors governs the quality of work management data, and ensures maintenance strategies, materials readiness, and schedule commitments are met. The Advisor drives continuous improvement through analysis of performance trends, BI insights, and equipment reliability indicators. Acting as a key support to the Maintenance Superintendent—this position plays a vital part in ensuring operational continuity, technical excellence, and long term equipment health.
Essential Duties
Provides senior technical leadership and end to end work management governance across the full workflow (identify → plan → schedule → execute → analyse).
Oversees prioritisation, plan approval, schedule sequencing, and data integrity to ensure efficient and effective execution.
Defines and optimises strategic maintenance tasks (PMs, inspections) based on performance and operational needs.
Reviews and endorses plans, verifying priorities, materials, labour, tooling, permits, and overall planning accuracy.
Ensures schedules are technically achievable, including resource levelling, equipment and material availability, and realistic timelines.
Acts as QA/QC authority and escalation point, validating complex work quality, procedural compliance, and completion standards, including follow-ups and corrective actions.
Owns KPI monitoring, BI insights, and continuous improvement initiatives, while leading Technical
Advisors & Supervisors and supporting the Maintenance Superintendent.
Training & Experience
Bachelor Degree in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent
Demonstrated experience within a in a similar role within the mining industry
Experience with crushing conveyors, grinding mills and large slurry pumps
A personal commitment to safety
Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 21/21 roster.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Apply

At Save the Children Australia, we attract bright and big-hearted people who are inspired to make a difference. Together, we are fearless in our pursuit of making lasting change for the children and communities who need it most.
The REnew Pacific GEDSI and Partnerships Coordinator is responsible for providing high quality technical support in Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion, child safeguarding, and locally led partnerships across all REnew funded grantees across the Pacific region. The role will ensure that implementing partners meet Save the Children’s standards on inclusive practices and safe programming and strengthen the capacity, systems, and leadership of local organisations delivering REnew activities.
Providing a critical bridge between Save the Children’s technical objectives and civil society, private sector, and government partners implementing Renew, the position will support partners to design and implement inclusive, equitable, and community driven interventions and contribute to Save the Children’s wider localisation and civil society strengthening agenda. This dedicated role will coordinate appropriate resources to meet site visit requirements with regular national international travel under the REnew project.
The position will also work closely with the Safeguarding Lead, Partnerships and GEDSI team, REnew program teams, and relevant government ministries.
Here your skills will be valued
Role requirements
Program Design and Technical Support
Provide technical advisory support to REnew grantees to strengthen gender equality, disability inclusion and social inclusion in program design and implementation.
Lead the completion of the Gender Equality Marker and Disability Sensitive Minimum Standards tools for partner activities.
Support partners to integrate child safeguarding and safe programming approaches into all stages of the project cycle.
Contribute to high quality concept notes and proposals related to REnew or new localisation and resilience initiatives.
Support partners to conduct participatory community consultations, ensuring the voices of girls, boys, women, people with disabilities and youth are represented.
Program Implementation and Quality Assurance

27199.description:
Summary
The role is responsible for overseeing all areas managed by Security Compliance and Safety Officers, including fleet security, corporate security, and OSH/risk management. This position ensures that all security and safety operations are compliant with relevant standards, effectively managing risks and maintaining high standards of Occupational Safety and Health (OSH). The individual will coordinate activities, provide guidance, and ensure consistent implementation of safety protocols across the organization. Depending on the organizational needs, the focus on specific areas may vary, requiring flexibility and adaptability.
Duties and Responsibilities
Leadership and Supervision:
Supervise and provide direction to Security Compliance and Safety Officers.
Coordinate and oversee the daily activities of security and safety personnel.
Ensure consistency in the implementation of security and safety protocols across all departments.
Prioritize and shift focus between fleet security, corporate security, and OSH/risk management based on current organizational requirements.
Compliance:
Oversee the compliance of all security and safety operations with relevant standards and regulations.
Conduct regular compliance audits and inspections across various departments.
Ensure up-to-date maintenance of compliance documentation and policies.
Risk Management and OSH:
Supervise the development and implementation of OSH policies and procedures.
Conduct comprehensive risk assessments and hazard analyses across all operational areas.
Oversee investigations of incidents and accidents, ensuring corrective actions are implemented.
Ensure all project sites and company premises are set up and maintained within OSH standards.
Supervise the works to ensure compliance with OSH standards and report immediately to the manager if any site or premise does not meet the required standards.
Training and Development:
Develop and coordinate comprehensive training programs for security and safety officers.
Organize regular drills and emergency response training sessions.
Provide ongoing professional development opportunities for the team.
Reporting and Documentation:
Maintain accurate records of security incidents, safety inspections, risk assessments, and compliance activities.
Prepare and present detailed reports on security and safety performance to senior management.
Ensure all documentation is compliant with legal and regulatory requirements.
Coordination and Communication:
Act as the primary point of contact between security and safety officers and senior management.
Facilitate effective communication and collaboration between different departments and teams.
Coordinate with external security agencies and law enforcement as necessary.
Job Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in Security Management, Occupational Safety, Risk Management, or a related field.
Certified Safety Professional (CSP) or similar certification preferred.
Minimum of 7 years of experience in security and safety management, with at least 3 years in a supervisory role.
Strong knowledge of relevant safety and security standards and regulations.
Experience in policing, security, or military preferred.
Martial arts skills preferred.
Valid driver's license and the ability to drive.
Strong leadership, analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
Ability to effectively manage and coordinate multiple projects and teams.
Flexibility to adapt and prioritize assignments in different areas as organizational needs change.
This role may require working in shifts, including nights and weekends. The supervisor may need to respond to emergencies outside of regular working hours. The working environment can be remote and may involve high-risk areas. The individual must be prepared to travel to various project sites and company premises as required to ensure compliance with OSH standards.
Required to travel to areas where needed.

[email protected]
.  Please include the Job ID "
#27199
" in the email's subject to ensure your application is processed.
Apply

About Christian Leaders Training College (CLTC)
The
Christian Leaders' Training College of Papua New Guinea (CLTC)
is an accredited, interdenominational theological institution established in 1964. Headquartered at its main residential campus in Banz, Jiwaka Province. CLTC operates multiple campuses dedicated to training men and women for Christian ministry and leadership across Papua New Guinea and the South Pacific. The college blends academic excellence with rigorous spiritual formation, serving a diverse community of students, faculty, and agricultural support staff unified by evangelical biblical truths.
CLTC is now recruiting for an experienced and dedicated People and Culture Manager to provide the leadership and effectively manage its Human Resource Department.
Position Title:
People and Culture Manager
Location:
Main Campus (Banz, Jiwaka Province, Papua New Guinea)
Reports To:
Vice Principal – Operations
Supervision:
People and Culture Officer/Payroll Officer
Position Type:
Full-time

To facilitate the strategic management, care, and development of CLTC's personnel. This role ensures that all human resource operations, recruitment, workforce development and workplace culture initiatives actively align with the college’s Christian mission and statement of faith.

Culture & Values Leadership:
Cultivate a supportive, Christ-centered work environment that mirrors CLTC's lifestyle expectations and statement of belief.
HRIS Optimization:
Manage, streamline, and serve as the primary administrator for the college's Human Resource Information System (HRIS).
Data & Payroll Integration:

Talent Acquisition:
Oversee the end-to-end recruitment lifecycle, including vacancy advertising, interviewing, selection, and vetting for organizational alignment.

Design and execute structured induction and orientation programs for faculty, support staff, and incoming volunteers.
Performance Management:
Coordinate the annual staff appraisal process, guiding supervisors to conduct fair, development-focused performance reviews.
Training & Development:
Conduct training needs analyses to implement professional development opportunities that enhance staff capabilities.
Employee Relations:
Provide proactive coaching, mentoring, and conflict resolution support to address employee grievances or disciplinary matters.

Christian Faith:

Thorough operational understanding of Papua New Guinea employment acts, labor laws, and industrial relations standards.

Excellent interpersonal, written, and cross-cultural communication skills suitable for a diverse multi-cultural workforce.

Integrity and professionalism.

27191.description:
Technician – Metallurgy
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
The New Porgera Limited now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our Processing Department as
Technician – Metallurgy.
About the role
Reporting to the Metallurgy Laboratory Supervisor, the successful candidate will undertake routine and non-routine work in the metallurgical plant laboratory and ensure the test work is completed with high standards and in a timely manner.
In this role, you will:
Ensure plant checks and monitoring related to cyanide and pH compliance are maintained including routine maintenance and operational checks for online instruments
Conduct plant checks and participate in all routine metallurgical tasks, plant surveys, sampling, inventory stock take and test work programs
Support Plant Mets and Met Lab Supervisor to carry out routine plant checks as well as involve fully to assist with plant troubleshooting when issues arise
Follow up on results with Assay Lab and ensure all plant and test data entries are updated and reported on time. This includes calibration data for online instruments
Ensure all tasks are done accurately and the relevant SOPs are followed correctly
Promote environmentally sound work practices among peers and contractors and ensure all environmental requirements are complied with and maintained
Uphold high standards of health and safety awareness, ensuring compliance with NPL’s Occupational Health & Safety Policy and all safety procedures.
About You
To succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experiences:
Tertiary qualifications with a Degree in Metallurgy
A recent graduate after 2019 with 2 to 3 years work experience is preferred however, any previous experience in the Metallurgy laboratory will be an advantage.
Sound communication skills and computer literacy in Windows applications (MS Word, Excel and Outlook)
Be highly motivated and willing to learn and train, share and pass on knowledge to others
The incumbent must be a team player, be highly organized and able to perform multiple tasks, paying attention to detail and meeting deadlines
Physically fit, can work long shifts when required and willing to be on a fly in fly out roster.
Solid understanding of workplace health and safety regulations, particularly in Processing plant
Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to collaborate across teams.
Proficient in using maintenance management systems and Microsoft Office applications.
Mobilization Requirement
This is a PNG National position, a site-based role on a FIFO arrangement with a rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off. Candidates must successfully pass a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening (to be arranged only for successful candidates after the interview stage), and provide an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months). Candidates must be PNG Nationals and available to start immediately. Females are encouraged to apply.
Join Our Team as a Technician – Metallurgy
Embark on a rewarding career with New Porgera Limited as a Technician – Metallurgy. This role offers a unique opportunity to work with a dynamic team to contribute to NPL’s success. Enjoy a balanced work schedule, competitive compensation, and a chance to develop your career and technical expertise in a supportive and professional environment.
Note:
This advert will be open until
5
th
of June 2026
. If you do not hear from NPL within next two (2) weeks following the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful for this opportunity.

Commercial – Procurement

27172.description:
TITLE
SENIOR WASH TECHNICAL OFFICER
REPORTING TO
WASH ADVISOR & DOTTED LINE TO WEWAK PROJECT COORDINATOR
LOCATION
WaterAid – Wewak sub office, East Sepik Province, Papua New Guinea
CLASSIFICATION
E
EMPLOYMENT DETAILS/HOURS
Permanent,
Three-year contract (subject to three months’ probation)
Introduction
WaterAid’s vision is of a world where everyone has access to safe water and sanitation. Our mission is to transform lives by improving access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) in the world’s poorest communities. WaterAid works with partners to maximise its impacts for policy change/influence.
WaterAid works through supporting local organisations and government authorities to design and demonstrate appropriate and sustainable WASH programs. WaterAid also seeks to influence policy change through government and other key sector actors to secure and protect the right of poor people to safe, affordable water and sanitation services.
Everything we do is shaped by our six values:
Integrity
Respect
Collaboration
Courage
Accountability
Innovation
WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners and the government to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive and climate resilient water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is on the National Capital District and Central Province in the Southern Region, East Sepik Province and East New Britain Province.
WaterAid works through supporting local organisations and government authorities to design and demonstrate appropriate and sustainable WASH programs. WaterAid also seeks to influence policy change through government and other key sector actors to secure and protect the right of poor people to safe, affordable water and sanitation services.
WaterAid is a child safe organisation. We recognise that we must meet community expectations, and the trust placed in our personnel to maintain the highest standards of conduct with children. Therefore, all positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.
WaterAid is committed to protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in everything we do. The values and standards we uphold are highlighted in our Global Code of Conduct. All positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Global Code of Conduct.
WaterAid passionately believes everyone in the organisation has a role to play in innovation, encourages curiosity about the world and empowering everyone to act. We recognise that both big and small changes can have positive impacts on our roles, our team and our mission.
WASH in PNG
Papua New Guinea (PNG) faces a severe WASH crisis, with some of the lowest access rates globally. Only 45% of the population has access to basic drinking water, 19% to basic sanitation, and 28% to household handwashing facilities with soap (JMP, 2024). WASH access in healthcare facilities (HCFs) is critically low, with 86% not meeting basic service levels (National Department of Health & WaterAid, 2021). Addressing these gaps is essential for improving public health, particularly for pregnant women and newborns.
The overarching goal of the Advancing Quality Universal Access to WASH in East Sepik Province (AQUA) project is to improve access to safe, clean and sustainable WASH and enhance health outcomes in East Sepik Province. By focusing on target districts, including Wewak district, the project aims to catalyze sustainable WASH system improvements, advancing the Wewak District WASH Plan (2024 – 2027). A particular emphasis on WASH in healthcare facilities will enhance the health and safety of patients and healthcare workers. Additionally, the project will strengthen the capacity, leadership and evidence base of the East Sepik Provincial WASH committee and Health Authority, supporting the future scale-up of essential WASH services.
Inclusive, Climate Resilient WASH in Wewak District, East Sepik, Papua New Guinea (TCCF 2024-2025): This is a continuation of WaterAid's WASH service delivery efforts in the Wewak District, East Sepik province, which has been ongoing for the past three years with support from TCCF (2021-2025). Our activities have primarily centered around increasing access to clean, safe, and reliable water sources, as well as offering appropriate sanitation and hygiene solutions to both communities and healthcare facilities.
By addressing critical WASH challenges, this project will contribute to sustainable, equitable water and sanitation access in PNG’s most vulnerable communities. The goal aligns with Country Strategy aim 2- WaSH in Public Health and increase the political will and commitment for them prioritise WaSH in Health Care Facilities ensuring the policy, practise and investment are aligned well.
